# Amaterasu — the app, running, on your machine

**Nature: Transmuter.** It runs declared machinery and a long-running local process; it writes no
code and sends nothing (a **deploy** is **G3**).

> **Build what I am working on and start it on the target I said, from the directory I actually work
> in, and tell me the exact command so I can run it myself.**

Phase four of `ren`, after [`kokusen`](../kokusen/SKILL.md); it never pushes or opens anything. **Every rule of the declaration it executes is
[`docs/LAUNCH-MIGRATION.md`](../../../docs/LAUNCH-MIGRATION.md) § *Launch declaration rules***.

## 0. Standalone entry

[`docs/STANDALONE-ENTRY.md`](../../../docs/STANDALONE-ENTRY.md) (§ 4 skip; plugin root per [PROCESS.md](../../../docs/PROCESS.md)). Cold adds **P1**–**P2**, read with § 3: a `ren` worktree turn reports without running, while explicit preview runs § 3b. **Launch reads disk, not commits**: name uncommitted paths.

## 1. Invocation

```
$amaterasu [<target>]        # <target> names a key of nen/contract.json → project.launch
```

With no argument the target is `nen/workflow.json` → `launch.default`. **There is no built-in default
and none is ever guessed** — a wrong build on a wrong device is not undone by relaunching. A
missing argument or configuration item is asked for and set up inline (`missing-argument`,
`missing-configuration`; [`WORKFLOW.md`](../../../docs/WORKFLOW.md) § 4 *Ask, set up, continue*), a
launch target set up through [`jujutsu`](../jujutsu/SKILL.md).

| What the declaration says | What amaterasu does |
|---|---|
| `project.launch` **absent** or **empty** | record `no launch target declared; skipped`, naming `nen/contract.json`, and continue |
| `launch.default` **`null`**, no argument, **no** declared targets | the same, naming `launch.default` |
| `launch.default` **`null`** but targets **are** declared, no argument | **the case that asks**, the declared targets as options |
| an argument naming an undeclared target | **the trigger to ask**: name it, the declared targets as options (or one set up through `jujutsu`), **never a near-match** |

**Asking on the no-launch case is the defect**: a question the configuration answered, asked every
`ren` turn, trains the maintainer to dismiss it — no question, stop or bell; continue.

**§ 1a · The profile.** Under `nen/workflow.json` → `profile` `fast`, [`ren`](../ren/SKILL.md) § 2a
skips this phase and the launch line reads `deferred by profile fast; isolation still requires an
explicit maintainer core-launch call` — nothing built or moved (mukai has no launch step).
Named by the maintainer, it runs under any profile.

## 2. The parameters, and the completion the launch owes

| Value | File → key |
|---|---|
| The default target and the disconnected-device fallback | `nen/workflow.json` → `launch.default`, `launch.fallback` |
| The targets — verb, args, device, after-steps, lane, artifact | `nen/contract.json` → `project.launch.<target>` (LAUNCH-MIGRATION) |
| The verb's command line, and where it runs | `project.verbs.<lane>.<verb>`, `project.lanes.<lane>.cwd` |

**`nen shu dev|run --target <name>` executes the whole block** — the probe, the lane's verb with
`args` appended, the after-steps with both substitutions. **With no `nen/workflow.json`**
([PROCESS.md](../../../docs/PROCESS.md) § *Invocation and parsing*) there is **no** `launch.default`
and **no** `launch.fallback`: with targets declared, name them and ask; with none, § 1's no-launch
case.

**Physical-device completion.** The lane must build for the target's **actual platform** — check the
dry run's lane, destination, artifact substitution and after-steps first. **An iPhone target
wired to a simulator build is an incomplete declaration** (a simulator `.app` named in `after[]` is no
device artifact): repair it within authorized scope or record the blocker through
[the discovery protocol](../../../docs/DISCOVERY.md). **Success is the device build, its install and
the launch, each reported**; a dry run or build-only result is **`launch incomplete`**, and missing
install/launch steps are a declaration gap even at exit `0`. **Record discovery is Nen's shared launch
resolver's** ([nen#204](https://github.com/zheref/nen/issues/204)); a temporary normalizer stays
**linked** with owner and removal condition; **no extraction key is added to an older binary.**

## 3. Core default for `ren`, § 3a validation, § 3b explicit worktree preview

**Ordinary and `ren` launches run from core** — never automatically from a `git worktree`, subagent copy or temporary clone, where uncoordinated builds race core on one port, derived-data directory or shared device.

**In a worktree during `ren`:** resolve core with `nen wc worktrees --repo <bound effort path> --json` and render `--repo <core> --target <name> --dry-run` only, keeping authoring bound to the worktree. Label it `core launch deferred; explicit maintainer call required`; quote any refusal/precondition verbatim; note core's tree may differ; never swap or run core automatically, and continue report/bell without asking. Only an explicit maintainer `$amaterasu` call authorizes launching core, and `$amenotejikara` is a separate swap call ([`senkaimon`](../senkaimon/SKILL.md) § 3 authorizes both for its queue). An original-prompt core-authoring waiver alone does not authorize either action; after either call, authoring, parity and delivery remain in the bound effort checkout under WORKFLOW § *Where worktrees live*. Before a core launch, `nen wc swap --status --repo <core>`: name an active swap; exit `1`/`2` refuses.

**§ 3a · Validating a declaration under review** from a non-core checkout ([`jujutsu`](../jujutsu/SKILL.md) § 6). Only when **all four** hold: written delegation **names device and target**; purpose is **declaration review**, never `ren` or a composite; **no other session holds the app**; and **the report states verbatim** — *"validation launch from a non-core checkout: `<path>`; delegation names device `<name>` and target `<key>`; declaration PR `<url>`"*.

**§ 3b · Explicit local preview from a selected worktree (`zheref/hatsu#617`).** When the maintainer explicitly requests a local preview of a selected checkout/worktree, run `node "$hatsu_root/scripts/amaterasu_preview.mts" --repo <selected> [--target <name>]`. It launches directly from `<selected>` (committed and uncommitted files on disk) with **0 core swaps**, preserving both checkouts' branches and edits. `ren`/automatic turns never enter § 3b (`--automatic` retains § 3 deferral). Before launching, the helper checks `--dry-run --json` preconditions, loopback TCP ports (`127.0.0.1` and `::1`), and `<git-common-dir>/.nen/amaterasu/sessions.json`, refusing occupied ports, devices or active sessions by resource name and leaving the existing session intact. Results report checkout, target and verbatim command (`amaterasu-preview-guard`). Everything outside § 3a and § 3b is forbidden for non-core launches.

## 4. Resolving the device, the dry run, and the command you paste

**The probe's three outcomes are LAUNCH-MIGRATION's**; what this skill does with each:

| Outcome | What amaterasu does |
|---|---|
| Present **and usable** | substitute its id into `{device.id}` in the after-steps |
| **Present but NOT usable** | **Refuse; never the simulator fallback** — it is plugged in, one tap from working. With `readyWhen`, **nen already refused at exit `5`** (device, state seen, states accepted): relay it and name the on-device step that closes it ([`jujutsu`](../jujutsu/SKILL.md) § 3). With **no** rule nen reports it resolved: read the probe's state column and **report the missing `readyWhen` as a declaration defect** |
| **Absent** | **Report it by name** — *"`<device.name>` is not connected; the probe saw: `<what it listed>`"* — then fall back to `launch.fallback`, saying so and naming it |
| Absent, `launch.fallback` `null` | say so and stop: plugging one in is an on-device act, picking another a guess |
| No `device` declared | straight to the dry run |

```bash
nen shu <verb> --repo <core working directory> --target <name> [--lane <lane>] --dry-run [--json]
nen shu <verb> --repo <core working directory> --target <name> [--lane <lane>]
```

- **`<verb>` is `project.launch.<target>.verb`, exactly** — `dev` or `run`, closed; nen carries no
  target across the two (the other is exit `2` naming the fix). With `--target`, **the declared verb
  is checked before the lane's seat**, so an exit `4` there is a **real** seat, quoted as one.
- Dry run and pasted argv: [PROCESS.md](../../../docs/PROCESS.md) § *Running a declared verb* —
  **copied, never re-typed**.
- **One bare line whether or not the target declares `args`** (nen appends them); **a `--lane`
  contradicting `project.launch.<name>.lane` is exit `2` naming both**.
- `dev`/`run` are **long-running**: `--json` without `--dry-run` is exit `2`, and **the launch is never
  backgrounded** to free the terminal — say the app is running and what holds it.
- **Exit codes** per `docs/personas/kurapika.md` § *The `shu` verbs*; here `1` is a declared step
  failing — **say which: build, install or launch** — hand authored-code failures to
  [`rasengan`](../rasengan/SKILL.md), a failed install or launch being incomplete delivery; `3` an
  excluded host, a **G5**, never retried; `4` a real seat, quoted, then the repository's documented
  command run and said; `5` the program not on `PATH`.
- **The after-steps are nen's**, in the same `--target` call, nothing by hand. **Quote the dry run's
  `substitutes:` line**, not `artifacts:` — what the child receives, not what the build produces.

## 5. Residue

See [PROCESS.md § Residue](../../../docs/PROCESS.md#residue-and-owned-dependencies). **Boundary ([HR-390](../../../docs/ROSTER.md#hr-390)):** § 3a's delegation, purpose and report wording; **§ 3a's third condition** (no other session holds the app) is [zheref/nen#536](https://github.com/zheref/nen/issues/536), complemented locally for § 3b previews by `.nen/amaterasu/sessions.json`. **Record discovery** is [zheref/nen#204](https://github.com/zheref/nen/issues/204); **device state without `readyWhen`** lapses when `jujutsu` writes the rule. **No default target**, **no `--` passthrough**, and **nen stops no long-running child**.

## 6. Authority and hard limits

- **Permitted:** run declared `build`/`dev`/`run`, device probe and `after` steps in core (or selected worktree via § 3b / validated declaration via § 3a); return checkout, target and verbatim command.
- **Not permitted:** `nen shu deploy --run` (**G3**, row `release-go`); push, commit, PR, label or release. **Not a gate**: disconnected device without fallback stops and reports; unsupported host (`3`) is the one **G5**.
- **Never launches from anything but the core working directory**, except under § 3a's four conditions (verbatim report) or an explicit maintainer local preview under § 3b; **never from a parallel effort**; **never enters § 3a from a composite**; **never enters § 3b without an explicit maintainer preview request or automatically in `ren`**; and **never swaps core** during § 3b.
- **Never falls back past a real resource conflict**, silently to a simulator, or to an undeclared device; **never invents a target**, or asks when declared (§ 1).
- **Never types an undeclared `shu` subcommand**, drops `--target` past exit `2`, substitutes commands, re-types from memory, omits declared `args`, or claims running on a dry run or unread exit.
